answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, externally priced token as collateral before it may transact. The registry treats each identity as a vertex, but limits its influence by the value at risk, not by the number of names it creates. A Sybil attacker must therefore buy and lock more tokens for every extra identity, tying up capital and paying fees; identities cannot multiply cheaply into a haven for fake votes or rewards. Like timber, that stake has an opportunity cost while locked and may be slashed for provable abuse.
